description: Mach-O 64-bit inspection (design §8.1) and Wasm core inventory (design §8.2) in the macho/wasm namespaces, reusing the coff.* helpers and element/redaction machinery. Fat/universal + 32-bit Mach-O and Wasm operand decode are OUT OF SCOPE: emit clear errors, not stubs. Depends on FEAT-001 (signatures). Independent of FEAT-002/003.
steps: Mach-O (§8.1): `const h = try r.takeStruct(std.macho.mach_header_64, .little);`. --file-headers: magic; cputype/cpusubtype via a manual switch (std.macho.CPU_TYPE_X86_64->"X86_64", CPU_TYPE_ARM64->"ARM64", else bare `0x{x}`) — NOT {t}; filetype via `fn machoFiletypeName(ft: u32) []const u8` switch (MH_OBJECT->OBJECT, MH_EXECUTE->EXECUTE, MH_CORE->CORE, MH_DYLIB->DYLIB, MH_BUNDLE->BUNDLE, MH_DSYM->DSYM, else "") printed as `name (0x{x})` with bare `0x{x}` fallback when empty; ncmds/sizeofcmds/flags. All element-gated + redaction-aware.

Mach-O load commands: iterate ncmds `std.macho.load_command` entries, advancing by cmdsize. For cmd == .SEGMENT_64 re-read `std.macho.segment_command_64` + its nsects x `std.macho.section_64` for --section-headers. For cmd == .SYMTAB re-read as `std.macho.symtab_command` and use symoff/nsyms/stroff/strsize to read the symbol + string tables for --symbols.

Mach-O unsupported variants: fat/universal (FAT_MAGIC/CIGAM) and 32-bit (MH_MAGIC) -> clear `"unsupported Mach-O variant"` error (the dispatcher only matches MH_MAGIC_64, so this is the handler guard), never a stub.

Wasm (§8.2): verify std.wasm.magic + std.wasm.version ([1,0,0,0]); --file-headers prints version. Walk the section sequence: each section is id: u8 (std.wasm.Section enum) followed by a LEB128 u32 size; print an inventory for --section-headers/summary (section name via {t} on the Section enum, size); for export/custom(name) sections list exported names where cheaply decodable. Full operand decode is OUT OF SCOPE.
Allocator discipline: single d.gpa with matching defer free/deinit; local arena for the Mach-O symbol-name table if needed (mirror coff.dumpObject).
acceptance_criteria: `sig test lib/compiler/objdump.sig` compiles clean under strict mode.
`sig objdump --file-headers <macho64>` prints cputype/filetype via name+hex (not {t}); --section-headers lists SEGMENT_64 sections; --symbols reads the SYMTAB tables.
`sig objdump --file-headers <wasm>` prints the version and a section inventory; a fat/32-bit Mach-O or an unsupported wasm construct yields a clear error, never a TODO stub.
verification: Manual: if a Mach-O 64-bit and a .wasm input are available in-env, run `sig objdump --file-headers`/`--section-headers` on each and confirm stable output; otherwise record the `sig test` pass + reason in findings.

IMPLEMENTED (const macho = struct {...}, replacing the FEAT-001 banner stub):
- `fn machoCpuName(cputype: std.macho.cpu_type_t) ?[]const u8`: CPU_TYPE_X86_64->"X86_64", CPU_TYPE_ARM64->"ARM64", else null (bare-hex fallback at the call site). cpu_type_t is c_int (plain integer), rendered via @as(u32,@bitCast(..)) -> NEVER {t}.
- `fn machoFiletypeName(ft: u32) []const u8`: MH_OBJECT->OBJECT, MH_EXECUTE->EXECUTE, MH_CORE->CORE, MH_DYLIB->DYLIB, MH_BUNDLE->BUNDLE, MH_DSYM->DSYM, else "" (printed `name (0x{x})`, bare `0x{x}` when empty). filetype is a plain u32, switch not {t}.
- `fn dump(d)`: variant guard re-peeks the 4-byte magic; MH_MAGIC_64 proceeds, MH_MAGIC/MH_CIGAM/MH_CIGAM_64/FAT_MAGIC/FAT_CIGAM/FAT_MAGIC_64/FAT_CIGAM_64 -> d.failParse("unsupported Mach-O variant (fat/universal and 32-bit are not supported)") (never a stub), else "not a Mach-O file (magic 0x{x})". Then `takeStruct(std.macho.mach_header_64, .little)`. File-type banner (§3) element-gated. --file-headers prints magic/cputype(name+hex or hex)/cpusubtype/filetype(name+hex or hex)/ncmds/sizeofcmds/flags, numeric fields via coff.fmtIntField so -s redaction applies.
- Load-command walk: cmd_off starts at @sizeOf(mach_header_64); per command seekTo(cmd_off)+takeStruct(load_command); cmdsize sanity-checked (>= sizeof load_command and in-bounds vs fr.getSize()); advance by cmdsize. cmd==.SEGMENT_64 (when --section-headers) re-reads segment_command_64 then nsects x section_64, printing `Segment,Section Addr Size Offset Align` (addr/offset .va, size .size via coff.fmtIntField). cmd==.SYMTAB (when --symbols) re-reads symtab_command and calls dumpSymtab.
- `fn dumpSymtab(d, sc, file_size)`: bounds-checks symoff/nsyms*sizeof(nlist_64) and stroff/strsize vs file size (d.failParse on overflow); reads the string table once into a gpa buffer (defer gpa.free); seeks to symoff and reads nsyms x nlist_64, resolving each name from n_strx via std.mem.sliceTo(strtab[n_strx..],0) with bounds guard, honoring --only-symbol via filterMatches; prints n_value (.va) + name. Strict allocator discipline (single d.gpa, matching defer free).

IMPLEMENTED (const wasm = struct {...}, replacing the FEAT-001 banner stub):
- `fn sectionName(id: std.wasm.Section) []const u8`: std.enums.tagName(Section,id) orelse "custom?" -- Section is a non-exhaustive enum(u8); `{t}` on an unknown id PANICS (FEAT-002 toolchain finding), so this routes through tagName, same guard pattern as elf.writeEnum.
- `fn dump(d)`: consumes+verifies std.wasm.magic and std.wasm.version ([1,0,0,0]) (clear errors on mismatch); file-type banner (§3) prints version; --file-headers prints the version word. When --section-headers or --summary: walks the section sequence (id:u8 Section enum + takeLeb128(u32) size), bounds-checking body_start+size vs fr.getSize(), printing `Id Name Size` (size .va/.size via coff.fmtIntField); for .@"export" sections lists exported names (LEB128 count, then per entry LEB128-len name + skip kind byte + LEB128 index); for .custom sections lists the leading name string. Advances via seekTo(body_start+size) each iteration so undecoded bodies are skipped cleanly. Full operand decode OUT OF SCOPE as required.
